references.text: The parallel account in Numbers describes the same event where the Israelites defied the Lord's command and went up into the mountain to fight against the Amorites, despite Moses' warning.
Samuel warns the people of the consequences of not listening to the Lord's voice, a theme repeated from Deuteronomy 1:43.
Isaiah speaks of a rebellious people who refuse to listen to the Lord's law, reflecting the Israelites' disobedience in the wilderness.
Jeremiah describes how the people did not listen to the Lord's voice and did not walk according to his law, similar to the event at Kadesh-Barnea.
The people did not obey the Lord's voice, a pattern of disobedience that goes back to the wandering in the wilderness.
The psalm describes those who were rebellious against God's word and despised the Most High's counsel, just as the Israelites did.
Moses reminds us that the Israelites were rebellious against the Lord's command, neither believing in him nor listening to his voice.
The warning against acting presumptuously and not listening to the priest or judge reflects the presumptuous rebellion in Deuteronomy 1:43.
Hebrews refers to the generation that was disobedient and rebellious in the wilderness, who could not enter into rest because of unbelief.
